correctness.rationale: Choose the positive-shift Fourier columns as an orthonormal basis and replace exactly two by corresponding negative-shift columns. The Gram matrix is an identity block plus a 2-column cross block L, hence its minimum is 1−||L||=1−sqrt(1−s_min(K)^2) for the two removed reference coordinates K. Geometric-sum evaluation yields |K| entries d,b,c and negative off-diagonal phase product, so s_min(K)=[sqrt(4d²+(b+c)²)−|b−c|]/2. For p=3, L has one row; the same singular-value identity still applies. With y=sin²g and v=y/(sin²β−y), the derivative F_y′(v)<0 follows from a positive quadratic with negative discriminant; v decreases as shorter separation grows, proving unique adjacency minimizer. d=1/(p sin g) and q=1/(3−4sin²g) increase with g, giving strict decrease of the adjacent lower bound as p increases and stated limit. Independent direct eigenspectrum computations for all separations p=3..30 matched the formula. Finite matrices corroborate, not prove, all-p claims.

final_claim: For every period p≥3 and sign pattern with exactly two negative quarter-shift columns, the smallest squared synthesis eigenvalue of the finite periodic shifted-sinc Fourier matrix equals 1−sqrt(1−eta_{p,l}²), where eta is an explicit 2×2 Cauchy-compression singular value. It is minimized exactly for adjacent negative columns; the sharp infimum over periods is 1−sqrt(1−4(sqrt13−1)^2/(9 pi²))≈0.166762438881.
limitations: No claim for 3 or more minority classes, nonperiodic sign patterns, or genuine two-index Gram model.
